newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: S.AFRICA MULLS BROADER SOURCES FOR BEEF IMPORTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA MULLS BROADER SOURCES FOR BEEF IMPORTS.

text.p: South Africa is considering importing beef from its neighbours in southern Africa instead of just from Europe, South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said on Tuesday.

"Because of historical reasons, South Africa had to look at the European markets. But now that we are a democratic government, we should start looking at what the region can offer instead of resorting to European markets," he told reporters in Harare.
Pahad led South Africa's delegation to a two-day meeting of the Zimbabwe-South Africa Joint Commission which ended on Tuesday.
"I believe that time has now come for my government to allow beef imports from the region and I believe that my government is now moving in the right direction," he said.
South Africa has over the years been importing beef from Europe while Zimbabwe, Namibia and Botswana have been exporting prime beef to the European Union (EU).

"Intra-regional trade must be expanded so that we are able as a region to develop our economies and make them stronger. It is only as a region that we can compete on the international market," Pahad said
Zimbabwe and South Africa, he said, should look at the issue further.
In a communique the joint commission said the two neighbours were committed to moving towards a zero tariff regime in agriculture.

"The joint commission urges relevant government officials dealing with negotiations on trade in agricultural products to urgently convene with a view of removing the 35 percent duty on Zimbabwean agricultural exports to South Africa," they said.
